I've been looking at the compiler's error and warning output and noticed that the formatting of "Hint" sections is inconsistent.

*   When a compiler diagnostic message has both a non-empty body text and a hint, there must be a blank line (empty line) between the body text and the 'Hint:' line in the rendered output.

*   Hint text in operator-type-mismatch messages must begin with an uppercase letter: the phrasing must use 'The [operator] operator can be used with [type]s' (capital 'T'), not 'the [operator] operator can be used with [type]s' (lowercase 't').

*   Hint text must be line-wrapped to fit within the standard display width used by the rest of the compiler output; long hint strings that would exceed this width must wrap to the next line at a word boundary.

*   When two consecutive error blocks appear in a single diagnostic output, there must not be an extra blank line within the body of the first error block beyond what the message requires.


**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.
I'll start by exploring the repository structure to understand the codebase and locate the diagnostic/error rendering code.

I've implemented the fix in source files only. Here's a summary of the changes addressing all four formatting requirements:

## Changes

**`compiler-core/src/diagnostic.rs`** — `Diagnostic::write`
- Added a blank line between the body text and the `Hint:` line when both are non-empty (**requirement #1**). Diagnostics with empty body text still render the hint directly, with no spurious leading blank line.

**`compiler-core/src/error.rs`** — `hint_numeric_message`
- Capitalized the message: `"the … operator can be used with …s"` → `"The …"` (**requirement #2**).
- Removed the trailing `\n`. That stray newline was producing a second blank line between consecutive error blocks; dropping it leaves exactly the one blank-line separator the output requires (**requirement #4**).
- Wrapped the message through `wrap(...)`, so hint text now line-wraps at word boundaries to the standard 75-column display width used elsewhere (**requirement #3**).

## Verification

I ran the affected tests with insta in read-only mode to observe the real rendered output:

- **Operator hint** (`multiple_bad_statement_expression_fault_tolerance`): now renders `Hint: The +. operator can be used with Floats`, and the double blank line between the two error blocks collapsed to a single blank line.
- **Hint field path** (`bits_pattern_requires_v1_9`): a blank line is now inserted between the message body (`…resulting in compilation errors!`) and the `Hint:` line.

`cargo build -p gleam-core` compiles cleanly. I did not touch anything under `tests/` (nor the committed `.snap` fixtures) — those will be updated by the verification system's test patches. I also cleaned up the transient `.snap.new` files the test runs produced.
